learning_outcomes.text: Be able to integrate into work teams.
Be able to solve problems related to material processing.
Be able to analyze and synthesize information on the nature, structure, and properties of materials.
Be able to manage the necessary information for selecting the appropriate material for each application.
Be able to describe the heat treatments and transformation processes applicable to different materials.
Understand the relationship between the nature, structure, processing, and properties of materials.

Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of the practical application of engineering, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of practical application of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical failure: fracture, fatigue, and creep
Practice 1.- The micrographic process in materials and micrographic study of a zinc-coated carbon steel.
Practice 2.- Strain hardening in austenitic stainless steel sheet. Annealing against plastic deformation.
Practice 3.- Martensitic transformation in steels. Tempering.
Practice 4.- Study of toughness in polymers.
Practice 5.- Material selection using computer software
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain at least 5 out of 10 points in the global averaged grade. In the first and second calls, a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for the final exam; if this minimum is not reached, the final grade for the course will be the final exam grade. Laboratory practices (15%) are not recoverable. The theoretical questionnaire (7.5%) and the partial written test (7.5%) can be recovered in the second call's final exam if the grade obtained during the course is less than 5 out of 10. In the extraordinary call for completion of studies, the final exam accounts for 100% of the grade with no minimum mark required.
